result.topic_en: A scholium restricting the study of a vibrating elastic rod to motions without longitudinal forces, considering only normal forces F, and recalling the preceding integrated equations from which the final fourth-order equation was derived, with a note that pinning the rod at points by styli leads to various cases to be treated next.
result.transcription:
) 111 (
Scholion.
§. 8. Quoniam igitur vires ſecundum ipſam virgae directionem agentes, quibus ea vel extenderetur vel comprimeretur, ad aequationem finalem magis complicatam perducunt, eas in hac tractatione penitus remoueamus, et noſtras inueſtigationes ad eos tantum motus reſtringamus, quos virga, ſiue a nullis viribus ſollicitata, ſiue a talibus tantum, quae in virgae directionem normaliter agunt, quas ſupra litera F deſignauimus, recipere poteſt. Ipſam vero virgam hic perpetuo naturaliter rectam et per totam longitudinem vbique aequaliter craſſam et aequaliter elaſticam ſtatuamus, easdem denominationes retinentes, quae hactenus ſunt deſcriptae. At quia aequatio finalis per duplicem differentiationem eſt orta, etiam praecedentes aquationes, quae ad eam deduxerunt, conſideraſſe iuuabit, quae ſunt:
$\text{I. } -Fx + \frac{cc}{2g}\int dx \int ds \left(\frac{ddy}{dt^2}\right) = -bc^4\left(\frac{ddy}{ds^2}\right).$
$\text{II. } -F + \frac{cc}{2g}\int ds \left(\frac{ddy}{dt^2}\right) = -bc^4\left(\frac{d^3y}{ds^3}\right).$
$\text{III. } \frac{cc}{2g}\left(\frac{ddy}{dt^2}\right) = -bc^4\left(\frac{d^4y}{ds^4}\right),$ ſiue $\frac{1}{2g}\left(\frac{ddy}{dt^2}\right) = -bcc\left(\frac{d^4y}{ds^4}\right),$
vbi in priores adhuc vis F, qua virga normaliter vrgeri poteſt, ingreditur, cuius ratio erit habenda, quando virga non omnino eſt libera, ſed in vno pluribusue punctis quaſi ope ſtyli eſt fixa, circa quem tamen ſit mobilis; vnde ſtatim intelligitur, virgam infinitis modis per tales ſtylos affigi poſſe, quibus eius motus diuerſimode temperetur; quos diuerſos caſus in ſequentibus accuratius euoluemus.
Proble-

items.quote: eas in hac tractatione penitus remoueamus, et noſtras inueſtigationes ad eos tantum motus reſtringamus, quos virga, ſiue a nullis viribus ſollicitata, ſiue a talibus tantum, quae in virgae directionem normaliter agunt, quas ſupra litera F deſignauimus, recipere poteſt.
items.english: Let us entirely remove these [longitudinal forces] from this treatment, and restrict our investigations only to those motions which the rod can receive either when acted on by no forces, or only by such forces as act normally to the rod's direction, which we designated above by the letter F.

items.quote: vnde ſtatim intelligitur, virgam infinitis modis per tales ſtylos affigi poſſe, quibus eius motus diuerſimode temperetur
items.english: whence it is at once understood that the rod can be fixed by such pins in infinitely many ways, by which its motion is variously modified.

items.quote: quos diuerſos caſus in ſequentibus accuratius euoluemus.
items.english: these various cases we shall work out more accurately in what follows.
